source.extractionNote: Full 'Component Metadata' template present and read in full — this spec has both structure and intent, unlike Notification Indicator.

summary: A thin line used to visually separate content into distinct sections or groups, such as list rows, cards, or menu items. Orientation sets whether the line runs horizontal or vertical. It's a static, non-interactive element with no content of its own, choose the orientation that matches the layout direction it needs to divide.

intent.horizontal: Use to separate stacked content in a vertical layout, like rows in a list or sections on a page.
intent.vertical: Use to separate side-by-side content, like items in a horizontal row or a toolbar.

anatomy.role: Sizes and clips the line. Fixed thickness on the cross axis (height for horizontal, width for vertical); the main axis resizes via constraints to fill its container.
1. Line — the only visible part. Renders as a horizontal or vertical stroke depending on Orientation, 1px thick (stroke/thin token).
anatomy._note: The vertical variant is the same LINE node rotated -90deg, not a second drawing.

table.What changes: Divider has no interactive states. Orientation is fixed at placement and never changes at runtime.

table.Description: None. Divider is a static visual element, it does not animate or transition between states or orientations.
Divider has no content slots. It renders only the separator line and holds no text, icon, or nested elements.

do: Choose Orientation to match the layout direction, horizontal to separate stacked content, vertical to separate side-by-side content.
Resize the instance to fill its container rather than leaving it at the default 320×1 (or 1×40) size, the line stretches with the frame.
dont: Don't use Divider as a spacing or margin mechanism, it's a visual line with no built-in padding, use layout gap for spacing between elements instead.

accessibility: Non-interactive and not focusable, Divider carries no keyboard or focus behavior of its own
In code, expose it with the platform's separator role (and an orientation attribute for the vertical variant) so assistive technology announces it correctly
Uses the border/default semantic token for its color, which resolves separately for light and dark mode, don't override it with a hardcoded color

table.Description: 1px, bound to the stroke/thin token, the same for both orientations.
Not fixed. Constraints on the internal line stretch it to fill the available width (horizontal) or height (vertical) when the instance is resized.
0px, bound to the radius/none token, hard edges on both orientations.
border/default token. Resolves to a light neutral gray in light mode and a darker neutral gray in dark mode, so it stays visible in both themes automatically.

visualReference.policy: No images are stored; every node deep-links into Figma so a shot can be pulled on demand and is never stale.

issues.detail: root's fixed-axis dimension is bound to stroke/thin as 'height' in the horizontal variant and as 'width' in the vertical variant — the extractor reports this as binding drift (present in 1 of 2 variants each), but it's the correct, axis-appropriate split: each orientation only has a cross-axis thickness to bind, not a real inconsistency.

The table's 'Default' column shows a small checkmark-style icon for the horizontal row and '-' for vertical — this is the metadata template's own default-value marker, not a component icon prop. Divider has no icon parts.

Every metadata section (States, Behavior, Content, Anatomy, Usage, Accessibility, Layout & Theming) is present and explicitly filled — States and Behavior say 'none' outright rather than being empty, so their absence is authored intent, not a gap in this extraction.
